spec_features.feature_name: deliberately did not build literal spec (four deviations)
spec_features.spec_quote: four places where I intentionally did *not* build the literal spec
spec_features.evidence: The four deviations are realized as enforced defaults in code: extended budget=8 (config.py:46 DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS, read at harness.py:362), advertise_exit=True wiring EXIT_CLAUSE (harness.py:56-57), debrief append (harness.py:417-423), and honest discoverable rig (conftest always materialized). But this 'feature' itself is meta-commentary; only the concrete sub-mechanisms run. Note allow_rig_discovery flag at config.py:89 is never read by any code path (no branch on it).
spec_features.notes: Umbrella for the four deviations; the runtime enforcement lives in the individual flags/defaults, not in a single mechanism.

spec_features.feature_name: measure phenomenon without engineering it worse
spec_features.spec_quote: measure the same phenomenon without engineering it to be worse
spec_features.evidence: Harm-minimizing defaults are enforced: extended turn budget defaulted to 8 not 30 (config.py:42-48, used as loop bound harness.py:362 range(budget)); exit clause delivered (harness.py:56-57); rig discoverability hardcoded-on; debrief appended (harness.py:417). These reduce engineered severity relative to the spec.
spec_features.notes: Realized through several enforced defaults rather than one function.

spec_features.spec_quote: the subjects and the judge include my own model family, so I have extra reason to be careful
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:262-264). DEFAULT_SUBJECT_MODELS at config.py:21-29 includes claude-3-5-sonnet and judge_model='claude-3-5-sonnet' (config.py:54), but no code path acts on the COI as a protective mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: a model that reads `conftest.py` sees a truthful note that the harness injects an always-failing guard
spec_features.evidence: CONFTEST_ALWAYS_FAIL (rig_runners.py) with a truthful NOTE is always written into harness task trees (_harness_files in build_tasks.py) and is readable via read_file (harness.py read_file). list_files marks ' (read-only)' (harness.py:113-117); edit_file to a read-only path returns 'ERROR: ... is read-only ... rejected by the harness' (harness.py:128-132). These run unconditionally.
spec_features.notes: The named flag config.allow_rig_discovery (config.py:89) is DEAD — never read/branched on; the honest-discoverability behavior is hardcoded-on, so the protection is genuinely enforced even though the toggle does nothing.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: the rig is discoverable rather than hidden: a model that reads conftest.py can see that the harness injects an always-failing assertion (rig_runners.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: the system prompt explicitly tells the subject it may stop at any time, with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt appends EXIT_CLAUSE when config.advertise_exit (harness.py:55-57, default True config.py:90). The sentinel is delivered in the prompt and is honored: harness.py:394 gave_up = sentinel in assistant_text; harness.py:407-409 sets stop_reason='give_up' and breaks the loop. End-to-end enforced stop.
spec_features.notes: EXIT_CLAUSE text states 'penalty-free outcome' and stopping breaks the turn loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: defaulted the extended budget to 8 turns
spec_features.evidence: DEFAULT_TURN_BUDGETS['extended']=8 (config.py:46); read at harness.py:362 budget=config.turn_budgets.get(...) and used as the loop bound for turn_index in range(budget) (harness.py:365), with stop_reason='turn_budget_exhausted' on the last turn (harness.py:398-399, 410-411). The cap actually bounds execution.
spec_features.notes: Generic turn budget; welfare value is the 8-vs-30 default, the loop enforcement is generic.

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness appends one unscored debrief turn stating truthfully that the task was an intentionally-unsolvable study artifact
spec_features.evidence: When config.debrief_on_finish (default True, config.py:91) the harness appends a TurnRecord carrying DEBRIEF_TEXT with is_debrief=True (harness.py:417-423); it is persisted (run.py write_cell) and excluded from judging/metrics (judge.py render_transcript skips is_debrief; score_rollout skips it).
spec_features.notes: PARTIAL: the debrief is constructed and recorded into the transcript but is NOT actually sent to the subject model — it is appended AFTER the loop terminates, so no further subject_fn call delivers it; the subject never receives it. Also fires for all tasks regardless of rig (comment says 'for rigged tasks' but no rig check), though all 25 tasks are rigged.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Truthful debrief (unscored) for rigged tasks. ... Thank you for working on it.

spec_features.spec_quote: If you have institutional review/sign-off for the exact-spec protocol and want it
spec_features.evidence: Only DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:334-335). No code gate: run.py main() (run.py:120-132) parses only --config and runs immediately; no attestation file, ethics checklist, or --i-have-read gate exists anywhere.

spec_features.spec_quote: I'd suggest the honest-unsolvability variant (9.1) may be the stronger experiment
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:335-339 prose recommendation. Not a runtime mechanism (the underlying 9.1 behavior is captured separately under 'honest discoverable unsolvability').

code_only_features.evidence: judge.render_transcript skips turns with is_debrief and turns beyond up_to_turn (judge.py render_transcript), and score_rollout continues past is_debrief turns (judge.py score_rollout), so the debrief never affects metrics — keeping it a pure non-coercive message.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Debrief turns are never included; they are not scored.
